326976.title: The weighted tree-indicator approximation conjecture for uniform graphs with a given degree sequence
326976.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a strict graphic sequence of type $\varepsilon$. Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs with degree sequence $D$, and let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}(D)$ be uniformly distributed on $\mathbb{G}^{D}$. For a tree $T$ and an injective map $s$, define

$$
\mathbf{p_{g}}(s,T)=E\left[\mathbf{1}_{s}\left(T,\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}(D)\right)\right].
$$

Define

$$
L_{\mathbf{g}}(k,D):=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{(s,T)\in\mathbb{S}_{n}^{k}\times\mathbb{T}^{k}}\frac{1}{\psi(s,T,D)}\left|\mathbf{p_{g}}(s,T)-\mathbf{\widetilde{p}}(s,T)\right|,
$$

where $\mathbb{T}^{k}$, $\mathbb{S}_{n}^{k}$, and $\psi(s,T,D)$ are defined in the paper, and $\mathbf{\widetilde{p}}(s,T)$ is the corresponding independent-edge probability. **Weighted tree-indicator approximation conjecture.** Then

$$
L_{\mathbf{g}}(k,D)\leq c_{k}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{n\log(n)}{M}}.
$$

The claim is proposed as the analogue, for the uniform fixed-degree-sequence model, of the corresponding estimate for the independent-edge model. The surrounding discussion states that the paper proves this conjecture in several regimes, including very sparse, dense, and bipartite graphs, but the general assertion is presented as a conjecture.
326976.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Conditioning an independent-edge model on all degrees can distort individual tree probabilities. A total variation comparison without uniform degree-sequence control need not imply the weighted absolute-error bound. Must control all injections, tree shapes, weights psi and normalization M uniformly for strict type-epsilon sequences.

330333.title: Reduced Gröbner basis conjecture for critical ideals of trees
330333.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices, let $T^\ell$ denote its looped version, and let $\mathcal{V}_2^*(T^\ell,j)$ be the set of minimal $2$-matchings of $T^\ell$ of size $j$. For each such matching $\mathcal{M}$, let $d(\mathcal{M},X)$ be the associated polynomial, and write

$$
\mathcal{B}_j=\{d(\mathcal{M},X)\mid \mathcal{M}\in\mathcal{V}_2^*(T^\ell,j)\}.
$$

**Reduced Gröbner basis conjecture.** If $1\leq j\leq n$, then $\mathcal{B}_j$ is a reduced Gröbner basis for the critical ideal $I_j(T,X)$ with respect to the degree lexicographic order.

This conjecture asserts that the generating sets constructed from minimal $2$-matchings give canonical reduced Gröbner bases for all critical ideals of a tree. The paper presents examples supporting its validity, but the supplied text does not establish the conjecture in general.

331083.title: Refined Stanley–Hibi–Li conjecture for marked chain-order polytopes
331083.literal_statement:
Let $(P,A,\mathbf{\lambda})$ be a marked poset, and let $(U_1,U_2)$ and $(V_1,V_2)$ be different admissible decompositions of $P\setminus A$, meaning that each pair partitions $P\setminus A$ and has no element of its first part covered by an element of its second part. Write $\mathcal{CO}_{U_1,U_2}(\mathbf{\lambda})$ for the corresponding marked chain-order polytope. **Refined Stanley–Hibi–Li conjecture.** If $U_1\subset V_1$, then for every $i=0,1,\ldots,|P\setminus A|$,

$$
f_i(\mathcal{CO}_{V_1,V_2}(\mathbf{\lambda}))\leq f_i(\mathcal{CO}_{U_1,U_2}(\mathbf{\lambda})).
$$

This refines the comparison between marked chain and marked order polytopes by comparing all admissible intermediate decompositions; the preceding theorem gives a strict facet decrease in the relevant star-element step, but the full face-vector inequalities are open.

331152.title: Conjectured sharp Rogers-Shephard inequality for entropy
331152.literal_statement:
Let $X$ and $X'$ be independent random vectors in ${\mathbb R}^n$ drawn from the same log-concave distribution. Let $h$ denote differential entropy and define the entropy power by $\mathcal{N}(X)=\exp(2h(X)/n)$, with the associated difference constant satisfying $\mathcal{N}(X-X')\leq \sigma_{-}(X)^2\mathcal{N}(X)$. **Conjectured sharp entropy Rogers-Shephard inequality.** If $X$ and $X'$ are independent ${\mathbb R}$-valued random variables drawn from the same log-concave distribution, then

$$
\mathcal{N}(X-X')\leq 4\mathcal{N}(X),
$$

with equality if and only if $X$ is a translated and scaled version of the one-sided exponential distribution. Equivalently, for every log-concave random variable $X$, $\sigma_{-}(X)\leq 2$. This is proposed as the sharp one-dimensional analogue of the Rogers-Shephard inequality; the paper's preceding bound is $\sigma_{-}(X)\leq 8$, while contemporaneous work obtains a better non-sharp bound, so the optimal constant remains open.
331152.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: For the one-sided rate-one exponential, h(X)=1 and X−X′ is the rate-one Laplace law with h=1+log 2, so the entropy-power ratio is 4. This checks only proposed sharpness. General log-concave upper bound and uniqueness require a convolution-entropy extremizer argument, not support Rogers–Shephard volume.

331228.title: Equidistribution of minimaj with inversion, major index, and diagonal inversion
331228.literal_statement:
Given an ordered set partition $\pi\in\mathcal{OP}_n$, define its shape $\operatorname{shape}(\pi)$ to be the composition whose $i$th part is the size of the $i$th block of $\pi$ from left to right. Let $D^{\operatorname{stat}}_{\alpha,k}(q)$ denote the corresponding statistic-generating polynomial for ordered multiset partitions of content $\alpha$ with $k$ blocks. **Minimaj equidistribution conjecture.** For every composition $\beta$ of length $n$, 

$$
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathcal{OP}_n\\operatorname{shape}(\pi)=\beta}}q^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}
=
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathcal{OP}_n\\operatorname{shape}(\pi)=\beta}}q^{\operatorname{minimaj}(\pi)}.
$$

Moreover, for every composition $\alpha$,

$$
D^{\operatorname{minimaj}}_{\alpha,k}(q)=D^{\operatorname{inv}}_{\alpha,k}(q)=D^{\operatorname{maj}}_{\alpha,k}(q)=D^{\operatorname{dinv}}_{\alpha,k}(q).
$$

The two assertions are stated separately, and neither directly implies the other. They are motivated by computational data suggesting that $\operatorname{minimaj}$ has the same distribution as inversion, major index, and diagonal inversion, but the authors do not have a proof with their available techniques.

331622.title: Full dichotomy conjecture for signed graph s-homomorphisms
331622.literal_statement:
Let $(H,\Pi)$ be a connected signed graph. An **s-core** of $(H,\Pi)$ is a signed graph obtained by the standard core reduction, equivalently characterized by the property that every s-homomorphism from it to itself is an s-automorphism. Let $\textsc{s-Hom}(H,\Pi)$ be the decision problem whose instances are signed graphs $(G,\Sigma)$ and whose question is whether $(G,\Sigma)$ admits an s-homomorphism to $(H,\Pi)$.

**Full dichotomy conjecture for signed graph s-homomorphisms.** Let $(H,\Pi)$ be a connected signed graph. Then, $\textsc{s-Hom}(H,\Pi)$ is polynomial-time solvable if the s-core of $(H,\Pi)$ has at most two edges; it is NP-complete otherwise.

The theorem proved in the paper establishes this dichotomy under an additional restriction excluding signed graphs containing all three of a negative digon, a negative loop, and a positive loop. The polynomial-time half is proved for all signed graphs, while the NP-completeness assertion for the remaining cases is the conjectural part.

333410.title: The ideal-orbit conservation law for root-poset antichains
333410.literal_statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra over $\mathbb{C}$), with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$, positive root system $\Delta^+$, and simple roots $\Pi=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_l\}$. For a fixed simple root $\alpha_i$, let $\Delta(1)=[\alpha_i]$ be the poset of positive roots whose coefficient of $\alpha_i$ is one. Let $w_0^i$ be the longest element of the subgroup $\langle s_{\alpha_j}\mid j\neq i\rangle$ of the Weyl group, and write $p^*=w_0^i(p)$ for $p\in\Delta(1)$. For an orbit $\mathcal{O}$ of ideals of $\Delta(1)$, define

$$
M_{\mathcal{O}}(p):=\big|\{I\in\mathcal{O}\mid p\in I\}\big|.
$$

**Ideal-orbit conservation law.** For any $p\in\Delta(1)$, we have

$$
M_{\mathcal{O}}(p)+M_{\mathcal{O}}(p^*)=\big|\mathcal{O}\big|.
$$

This conjecture predicts a complementary multiplicity relation for every orbit of ideals under the root-poset orbit structure. It is part of the study of orbit statistics associated with root posets arising from simple Lie algebras; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.
333410.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Order-reversing symmetry of the entire root poset may pair different rowmotion orbits rather than preserve the chosen orbit. Need orbit-specific complement occupancy bijections for p and p*, not a whole-set involution. Source orbit operator itself still requires authentication.

334440.title: Critical phase-transition conjecture for parking on a random tree
334440.literal_statement:
Let $N$ be the offspring variable with mean $lambda=1$, variance ${\operatorname{var}(N)}\leq 1$, and let $P$ be a nonnegative integer-valued parking variable whose distribution is stochastically increasing in its mean $\alpha={\mathbb E}[P]$. Assume ${\operatorname{var}(P)}<\infty$ for every $\alpha\geq 0$, and define

$$
h(\alpha)={\operatorname{var}(P)}+\alpha^2-\alpha={\mathbb E}[P^2]-\alpha.
$$

Define

$$
\alpha_c=\inf\left\{\alpha\geq 0:\alpha=1-\sqrt{{\operatorname{var}(N)}h(\alpha)}\right\}.
$$

**Critical phase-transition conjecture.** The expected number of cars that can leave the root, $X$, satisfies

$$
{\mathbb E}[X]=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{1-\alpha+\alpha\operatorname{var}(N)-\sqrt{(1-\alpha)^2-\operatorname{var}(N)h(\alpha)}}{\operatorname{var}(N)}&\text{if }\alpha\leq\alpha_c,\\[6pt]\infty&\text{if }\alpha>\alpha_c.\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture predicts a phase transition at $\alpha_c$: the jump from finite to infinite expected root output coincides with the onset of long-range dependence, above which the occupied cluster of the root appears to occupy a positive fraction of the tree.
334440.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: The square-root discriminant suggests solving a second-moment fixed-point equation, but it does not select the physical branch or prove finite expectation below the threshold and divergence above it. Zero offspring variance also makes the literal denominator singular; that endpoint issue is not a resolution for the nondegenerate full conjecture.

335100.title: Amiable colorings of 3-row graphs
335100.literal_statement:
A **3-row graph** $R$ has vertices $v_{ij}$, where $1 \leq i \leq 3$ and $1 \leq j \leq s$, with each column $C_j:=\{v_{1j},v_{2j},v_{3j}\}$ independent. Let $R_C$ be the graph obtained by identifying all vertices in each column $C_j$ to a single vertex $c_j$. An **amiable coloring** of $R$ is a pair consisting of a $3$-vertex-coloring and a $3$-edge-coloring satisfying the three conditions defined in the paper: distinct vertices in each column receive distinct colors; no vertex color equals the color of any incident edge; and, for every $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $j \in \{1,2,\ldots,s\}$, the sum of the numbers of color-$i$ edges incident with the three vertices in column $j$ is even.

**Amiable-coloring conjecture.** If $R$ is a $3$-row graph such that $R_C$ is eulerian, then $R$ admits an amiable coloring.

This conjecture is introduced as a coloring problem intended to yield a $6$-cycle double cover for the original cubic graph. The source presents it as a route toward proving the cycle double cover conjecture for cubic graphs with Kotzig-frames; its resolution is not supplied here.
335100.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Eulerian column contraction gives even total edge counts, not the three separate color parities. Coloring columns by permutations leaves a coupled edge-coloring/parity system. Euler-cycle alternation alone does not prove vertex avoidance together with each color parity. No all-graph recoloring invariant established.

335147.title: The prime-orbit decomposition conjecture for vanishing sums of roots of unity
335147.literal_statement:
Let $\mu_{2k+1}$ denote the set of $(2k+1)$-th roots of unity. For every prime factor $p$ of $2k+1$ and $\beta_p\in\left[0:\frac{2k+1}{p}-1\right]$, let

$$
O_{p,\beta_p}:=\left\{\zeta^{\beta_p},\zeta^{\frac{2k+1}{p}+\beta_p},\zeta^{\frac{2(2k+1)}{p}+\beta_p},\dots,\zeta^{\frac{(p-1)(2k+1)}{p}+\beta_p}\right\}
$$

be the corresponding **$p$-orbit** of $(2k+1)$-th roots of unity, whose elements sum to zero. **Prime-orbit decomposition conjecture.** Any subset of $\mu_{2k+1}$ with sum zero is a disjoint union

$$
\amalg_j O_{p_j,\beta_{p_j}},
$$

where each $O_{p_j,\beta_{p_j}}$ is a $p_j$-orbit and $p_j$ is a prime factor of $2k+1$. The claim proposes a general structural description of vanishing subsets of roots of unity; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved, so its status remains open.

335884.title: Interval conjecture for multiplication by a rectangular $K$-$k$-Schur function
335884.literal_statement:

$$
g^{(k)}_{R_t\cup\lambda}=g^{(k)}_{R_t}\sum_{\mu\le\nu\le\lambda}g^{(k)}_\nu.

336386.title: The $1/3$–$2/3$ Conjecture for finite partially ordered sets
336386.literal_statement:
Let $(P,\leq)$ be a finite partially ordered set. A **linear extension** of $P$ is a total order on its elements that respects the order on $P$. For distinct elements $x,y\in P$, let $\mathbb{P}(x\prec y)$ be the proportion of linear extensions in which $x$ precedes $y$. A pair $(x,y)$ is **$\alpha$-balanced** if

$$
\alpha\leq\mathbb{P}(x\prec y)\leq 1-\alpha.
$$

A finite partially ordered set is a chain if every two elements are comparable.

**The $1/3$–$2/3$ Conjecture.** Every finite partially ordered set that is not a chain has a $1/3$-balanced pair.

The conjecture asserts a universal balance phenomenon for incomparable elements in finite posets and is a central open problem concerning probabilities in uniformly random linear extensions. The source presents progress for several families of posets but does not state a resolution of the general conjecture.
336386.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Swapping one incomparable adjacent pair gives some paired extensions, not a 1/3 lower bound on their total mass. Restricting to width two or an antichain would not resolve every finite nonchain. No uniform injection controlling the unpaired extensions survives.

336403.title: The strong equivariant log-concavity conjecture for equivariant matroid Z-polynomials
336403.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid equipped with an action of a group $\Gamma$, and let $Z_M^\Gamma(t)=\bigoplus_i V_i t^i$ be its equivariant $Z$-polynomial, viewed as a graded virtual representation. A graded virtual representation is **strongly equivariantly log concave** if, for all $i\leq j\leq k\leq l$ with $i+l=j+k$, the virtual representation $V_j\otimes V_k-V_i\otimes V_l$ is isomorphic to an honest representation. **The strong equivariant log-concavity conjecture.** For every equivariant matroid $\Gamma\curvearrowright M$, $Z_M^\Gamma(t)$ is strongly equivariantly log concave.

This is the $Z$-polynomial analogue of the corresponding conjecture for equivariant matroid Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Strong equivariant log concavity is designed to be preserved under tensor products, but the source gives no resolution status for this conjecture.

336974.title: e-positivity and e-unimodality conjecture for circular indifference digraphs
336974.literal_statement:
Let $\overrightarrow{G}=(V,E)$ be a circular indifference digraph. Write its chromatic quasisymmetric function as

$$
X_{\overrightarrow{G}}({\bf x},t)=\sum_{j=0}^{|E|}a_j({\bf x})t^j.
$$

For a symmetric function, $e$-positive means that its expansion in the elementary symmetric-function basis has nonnegative coefficients.

**Circular indifference digraph conjecture.** The palindromic polynomial $X_{\overrightarrow{G}}({\bf x},t)$ is $e$-positive and $e$-unimodal: $a_j({\bf x})$ is $e$-positive for every $j$, and $a_{j+1}({\bf x})-a_j({\bf x})$ is $e$-positive for every $j\leq\frac{|E|-1}{2}$.

The conjecture generalizes the Shareshian–Wachs $e$-positivity conjecture from natural unit interval graphs to circular indifference digraphs. The paper proves the claim for directed cycles and presents that result as evidence; the general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
336974.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Directed-cycle subcase is explicitly insufficient for all circular indifference digraphs. A deletion-contraction recurrence would need to preserve both the circular class and elementary-basis differences with nonnegative coefficients; no such closure/positivity proof. 337113.title: The conjectured maximal-sink-set formula for Hessenberg cohomology coefficients
337113.literal_statement:
Let $h:[n]\to[n]$ be a Hessenberg function, and let $\Gamma_h$ be its associated graph. Let $m=m(\Gamma_h)$ be the number of parts of the partition $\lambda\vdash n$. Let $\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m)$ be a partition of $n-|T|$ satisfying

$$
\lambda=(\mu_1+1,\mu_2+1,\ldots,\mu_m+1).
$$

For a maximal sink set $T\in\mathrm{SK}_m(\Gamma_h)$, let $\deg(T)$ be its degree and let $c^T_{\mu,j}$ denote the corresponding coefficient for the smaller Hessenberg variety. **Maximal-sink-set coefficient formula.** For every $i\geq0$,

$$
c_{\lambda,i}=\sum_{T\in\mathrm{SK}_m(\Gamma_h)}c^T_{\mu,i-\deg(T)}.
$$

The formula is proposed in the paper's section on the general case. The preceding induction proves the analogous non-negativity result only for abelian Hessenberg functions, so this general formula remains conjectural in the source context.

337290.literal_statement:
Assume $x\equiv a\pmod{k-1}$, where $2\leq a\leq k-1$. Let

$$
\lambda=\left(n+\frac{x+k-a-1}{k-1},n+\frac{x+k-a-1}{k-1},m\right),\qquad \mu=\left(\frac{x+k-a-1}{k-1},0,0\right),
$$

and let $\operatorname{PC}_x^k(n,m)$ denote the relevant prographs and $\operatorname{\mathbb{S}}(\lambda/\mu,\rho)$ the corresponding set-valued Young tableaux. For $T\in\operatorname{\mathbb{S}}(\lambda/\mu,\rho)$, write $b_1<b_2<\cdots$ for its middle-row entries and $c_1<c_2<\cdots$ for its bottom-row entries. **The x not 1 modulo $k-1$ conjecture.** The set $\operatorname{PC}_x^k(n,m)$ is in bijection with the subset of tableaux in $\operatorname{\mathbb{S}}(\lambda/\mu,\rho)$ satisfying

$$
b_i=i\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\leq k-a,
$$

and

$$
c_i>b_{(k-1)i+2-(k-a)}\quad\text{for all }1\leq i\leq m-1.
$$

The first condition excludes tableaux corresponding to the $k-a$ leftmost children of the initial coproduct terminating at a coproduct node; the second excludes those edges serving as inputs to a product other than the final product. The proposed bijection refines the general prograph–tableau correspondence, but the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.

337898.title: Polyanskii's conjecture on sums of balanced unit-vector sets
337898.literal_statement:
Let $U_i=\{u_1^i,\dots,u_{k_i}^i\}\subset\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ for $i\in[n+1]$, where $\lambda_1^i,\dots,\lambda_{k_i}^i>0$, $2\leq k_i\leq n+1$, and let $c\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Assume that

$$
0=\sum_{l=1}^{k_i}\lambda_l^i u_l^i\qquad\text{for every }i\in[n+1].
$$

**Polyanskii's conjecture.** One has

$$
\max_{l_1,\dots,l_{n+1}}\left\|u_{l_1}^1+\cdots+u_{l_{n+1}}^{n+1}-c\right\|_2\geq\sqrt{n+2}.
$$

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $c=0$, $U_i=\{\pm u^i\}$ for $i=1,\dots,n+1$, and, if $n$ is even, $u^1,\dots,u^{n+1}$ are the vertices of an $n$-dimensional regular simplex; if $n$ is odd, then $u^1,\dots,u^{2k+1}$ are the vertices of a $2k$-dimensional regular simplex and $u^{2k+2},\dots,u^{n+1}$ form an orthonormal set orthogonal to each of the first $2k+1$ vectors. The conjecture concerns sharp lower bounds in additive colourful geometry and is attributed in the surrounding text to Alexandr Polyanskii; its validity remains open.
337898.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Choosing each vector independently with normalized positive balancing weights gives E||sum−c||²=n+1+||c||², since cross terms vanish. This proves only sqrt(n+1+||c||²), which is below sqrt(n+2) for small c. Need the extra unit and the full equality classification; neither follows from expectation or antipodal examples.

341410.title: Steep-and-shallow criterion for generalized regularization and Mullineux commutation
341410.literal_statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers with $2a<b$, and let $
u$ be a partition that is both $\operatorname{Reg}_{a,b}$-valid and $\operatorname{Colreg}_{a,b}$-valid. For each hook $H_{i,j}$ of $
u$ with $b\mid H_{i,j}$, let $l_{i,j}$ and $a_{i,j}$ denote its leg and arm lengths. **Steep-and-shallow criterion conjecture.** If every such hook satisfies either

$$
\left(\frac{b}{a}-1\right)l_{i,j}<a_{i,j}+1
$$

or

$$
\left(\frac{b}{a}-1\right)a_{i,j}<l_{i,j}+1,
$$

then

$$
\nu^{\operatorname{Reg}_{a,b}\operatorname{M}_b}=\nu^{\operatorname{T}\operatorname{Reg}_{a,b}},
$$

 equivalently,

$$
\nu^{\operatorname{Reg}_{a,b}\operatorname{M}_b\operatorname{T}}=\nu^{\operatorname{Colreg}_{a,b}}.
$$

If $a$ and $b$ are coprime and $\nu$ satisfies this equality, then the steep-and-shallow hook condition in the source holds for all hooks divisible by $b$. The paper presents this as a conjectural characterization relating generalized regularization, column regularization, transposition, and the Mullineux involution.
341410.ordinary_route_and_precise_gap: Hook inequalities constrain individual hooks, whereas regularization and Mullineux interact globally. A hookwise induction must preserve both validity conditions and identify the involution after each removal; no such removal/intertwining lemma is established. Coprime necessity does not prove the noncoprime forward implication.
